actions.name: policy.baselines.validate
actions.checks: An installation-aware validation or dry run needs reads of every referenced resource and affected device. Pure decoded/offline validation is exempt under caller-owned input authority; schema acceptance supplies no native execution or evidence guarantee.
actions.note: Validation and dry-run details require read permissions for referenced resources and every affected device.

exemptions.authority: Login, logout, getSession, own approval status and self-service re-authentication use authenticated subject ownership. In docs/specs/console-foundation.md section 6, locale/theme/density changes, local preference storage, navigation and Reload use the browser user's local state authority, with no server session or administrative data. Browser print of already authorized report rows (docs/specs/report-template.md section 4.1) uses the reader's local copy; any new fetch retains report/source checks.

Enrollment, renewal, ACME and SCEP use channel-specific principals, token or account bindings and jobs authorization; administrative issuance and approval still require their catalogue entries. Ed25519 CSR/chain checks and key replacement under enrollment, renewal, ACME and SCEP (docs/specs/ed25519-key-admission.md section 5) retain each channel's proof of possession and issuance principal. A valid public key or imported certificate alone grants no trust, enrollment or operator issuance authority.

Ordinary ingest, correlation, export, hold capture and retention workers use their narrow service authority. Operator promotion, replay, backfill and hold changes require the named permissions. In docs/specs/report-template.md section 4, scheduled runs use the owner's current events.reports.run and source rights; lost rights pause with audit, notifier workers send links only and retention workers expire availability under the approved installation setting. In docs/specs/export-destination-schema.md sections 2 through 5, jobs materializes approved defaults, resolves frozen secret revisions and delivers under current committed destination authority; resolution never authorizes a credential change or disclosure.

First-start setup and sealed offline custodian recovery use one-time setup or quorum authority, never a console permission. docs/specs/ed25519-key-admission.md section 5 keeps custodian-manifest acceptance/update, quorum signatures and sealed restore under offline-root, pinned distinct-custodian quorum and live-journal authority. Validate every key and the complete required inventory; invalid keys cannot lower the threshold, normalize authority or reopen service.
Local installation or repair with a signed OS package, direct OS removal and user warn dialogs use local OS or endpoint authority; they do not grant console access.

Host-provided MaxMind files, ingest partition caps, database durability and storage configuration require deployment authority. No platform.settings permission grants host, database or cloud administration. Connector deployment/network policy and publisher signing (docs/specs/extension-manifest.md sections 2 and 5) use the deployment operator's infrastructure authority and publisher's signing key respectively; neither grants Ricevanta install or registration authority. Local role/journal/audit/device/release key loading and trust validation (docs/specs/ed25519-key-admission.md section 5) use the owning service, deployment, release or offline custody authority; invalid-key replacement retains that owner's authorized flow. No generic key-repair or raw-secret-read permission follows.

Excluding compromised hosts, revoking external credentials and gateway-side secret cutover require the relevant host, CA or gateway authority. Ricevanta registration writes and certificate issuance retain their catalogue checks.
Apple portal renewal and vendor CSR signing require the external account or signing key. Ricevanta CSR creation, certificate upload and topic replacement retain separate permissions.

Lab execution, retained qualification evidence and independent reviewer decisions are development/release activities, not console administration permissions. Pure offline/decoded validation in docs/specs/export-destination-schema.md sections 6 and 9, docs/specs/extension-manifest.md sections 2 and 6, docs/specs/mdm-resource-schemas.md sections 6 and 7, and docs/specs/report-template.md sections 4.1 and 5 processes caller-owned content and static metadata under local process authority, with no installation reads or writes. This exemption does not cover installation-aware API validation. Schema/catalogue revisions, console build/dependency exceptions and CSP tests (docs/specs/console-foundation.md sections 2 through 7; docs/design/console.md sections 1 and 6.3), and the permission refresh (docs/specs/permission-catalogue.md section 7) use repository review and release authority, not console approval. Ed25519 point validation and DSSE checks (docs/specs/ed25519-key-admission.md sections 2 through 4; docs/specs/dsse-envelope.md sections 5 and 7) are bounded local cryptographic checks and confer no key trust.

Compiled policy actions, inventory changes and directory sync use their constrained protocol authority; manual writes, governed-pack re-enable and approvals retain catalogue requirements. Native convergence, generated configuration, approved repository resolution, collector calls, update/reboot scheduling, encryption and derived group membership in docs/specs/mdm-resource-schemas.md sections 3 through 5 run only under committed policy, exact content/target approval and constrained native/core authority. Inventory-driven expansion and required-set weakening still require the owning policy/group checks. Schema acceptance grants no live command, disclosure or native qualification.

An external CA performs its own issuance or revocation under its authority. Ricevanta reconciliation uses pki.external_issuance.reconcile and device or infrastructure certificate revocation keeps its separate immediate permission.

Encoding and scanning borrowed segment bytes are file-free library calls, not console or administrative API actions. The codec grants no file access, truncation, upload or acknowledgement authority; native durability and the spool manager remain separate gates. docs/specs/agent-batch-writer.md sections 2 through 7 add file-free sealing/compression of caller-owned bytes under local library-call authority. No seal result authorizes upload, deletion, repair or epoch changes; those remain local core and authenticated transport duties. The references in docs/design/agent.md section 5 and docs/design/events.md section 2.4 add no operator action.

Startup recovery uses the local core spool manager under exclusive segment ownership. Only TailIssue permits truncation to valid_len under exclusive ownership; native durability must be established before resuming at next_sequence. Fatal errors permit no truncation. This automatic local process grants no operator permission.

Sequence assignment and startup segment recovery use the local core pipeline authority, not an operator endpoint. Recovery results do not authorize remote repair or bypass the spool manager ownership and durability gates.

Declaration parsing, loading and environment lookup are bounded in-process metadata operations, not administrative actions. Catalogue revisions require development and release review. Policy edits, import and publication retain their catalogue permissions, approval and signing checks; the loader grants no publication authority.

Declaration and certificate-evidence checks run inside compilation and admission under existing policy and gateway authorization. They add no operator action or permission to override failed evidence checks. Policy publication and gateway or scope writes retain their catalogue permissions and consumer gates.
